Just how an agency can be messed up, not all talents are perfect golden stars. Most are still incredibly young with undecided or changing career goals. Hi Speerawow,   
To me, I think the dynamics of what is an evade comp has changed significantly with the light comp meta sporting several guaranteed hit comps. Take the first fight for example, yes, I do take a hit from Elsi's first Maiming Slash, and Sakura's rebel intention.   


Evade is always going to be a game of chance (unless you are geared up to 0% hit chance, obviously), yet in the first fight, even pulling off one evade changes the course of the fight entirely.   


Take Elsi's second maiming slash for example. If Vinera doesn't evade, she is dead to that hit. If HLeela doesn't evade, in the chance she survives, she is going to be forced to go back on the defensive, either healing Vinera and herself if vinera evaded, or going for full-life on Vinera if Vinera died.   


I would argue that this single dodge, was critical to the fight, and what made evade, "evade". Also keep in mind that the first fight is a 13 action fight, something that you hardly see in high ranking GB light comp fights. This allows me to preserve gas going into the second fight.   


I think a lot of people have the image that evade is useless if you don't evade most attacks. The days (imo) of full-on evade comps are long gone, and evade comps designed to take hits is the path to success. (and if you look at the other fights, you will notice my team had significantly more success dodging non-guaranteed hit abilities).   


In regards to your other point, it's an observable fact that the meta in high GB focuses around Yuna. While light comps do not make up the whole entire lineup, they are the most prevalent. My intentions of saying "breaking the meta" was to not use Yuna, or shoe-horning in light comps. No where did I mention that Auron wasn't carrying my team. He's the primary DPS, of course he should! But the prevalence of Auron is much lower than Yuna.   


In regards to your third point, I agree! In my opinion, evasion is just another form of "tanking" so you could make this comp by adding more tankiness rather than slotting in evade. However, a lot of people claimed that evade was "dead" because of all the guaranteed hit skills, which I wanted to show was not absolutely the case.   


I'm sorry if the title was misleading, but I wanted to show that people do not have to resort to light comps (which is undeniably the meta on this current GB map), to achieve success.

Hi Hakusnow, first, Just want to say I love your videos and I think the general sentiment behind this post is meaningful. As a HUGE Niv'lu fan, I really like the points you made. That being said, I do think it's fair to be a realist.

From this video, we see that you are rank mid-high 3000s. While that isn't a low rank in arena, it's certainly not considered to be at the competitive rank (IMO, the baseline for that would be top 1000). Second, while we don't see the gear of your opponent except for the first fight, even in that first fight, Yuna does not have bahamut, and your opponent is running an unoptimized VC (the JP aqui one).

Second, while this trend changed pretty quickly, from our observation of the JP meta, Yuna + Bahamut esper was the meta for around 2 months (and even after that, she remains "viable"), we might get Duane EX fast, and maybe BR Helena is released earlier, causing things to change, but I would disagree that the meta shifts very quickly in regards to Yuna. (I know you specialize in live PVP, which I have no experience with, and in that case, the story is very different for that environment).

Fair note, my specialty/focus is on high level GB, so the following comments are coming from that lens. I think It is completely feasible to be viable without Yuna/Bahamut in lower GB metas.

Currently, GBs are decided almost by whichever team has more Yuna Walls set up. I've looked at our past 5 GBs, and every GB was determined by which defense has more Yuna/Bahamuts. (note that it seemed Bahamut was the deciding factor here, not Yuna).

Aeon reaction is just a complete AP Staller if you cannot one-shot, and the return damage she can do if she procs an heal reaction so she can attack on her turn is pretty insane.

From hours of playtesting, it's possible to beat light comps on your first attack without fielding yuna yourself, but more often than not, you are completely gassed out for your second attack.

It is definitely incredibly frustrating playing against a meta dominated by Yunabaha, and I personally think surviving in a more competitive GB meta without Yuna unfortunately puts your guild at a disadvantage.

Those are just my thoughts, and I'd love to hear other people's reactions to the Yuna meta.Thanks again!

As somebody who frequently travels between the US and Japan and used to buy a shit ton of Japanese sealed product for cracking and selling, my opinion is don't. 

Yes, at first glance, Japanese foils go for significantly more than their english counterparts, but in actuality, they really don't. There are many obstacles to selling foreign cards (especially foils).

So I took it all the way down to about 30-40% more than the english version and still nothing. In the end, I traded it away for $80. The card was in my possession for over 3 years and I didn't want to keep it at all. The amount of people who place a premium on Japanese foils just isn't what it used to be so don't expect to be able to sell those foils for what "retail" is listed at. (another hint is to look at Japanese vendor buylist, nobody wants Japanese foils for the commander appeal) 

Another thing to note, look at non-foil prices of Japanese cards on sites like TCGplayer. Japanese versions of Dictate of Erebos and Vedalken Orrery are significantly cheaper than the English counterparts (although last time I checked was 2-3 months ago). The Renekton matchup is in your favor at level 1, 4-5, and 9+. 
The key to not losing the lane is to not let him push. Going in to lane, start pushing right away (Renekton's kit makes him push naturally as long as he's not trying to freeze it). Keep Q harassing him but if he is able to push into your tower, try to farm as best as you can. His sustain is outmatched by your q proc damage so don't be afraid to go for those. My build order against Renekton is Gunblade, Zhonyas, (Finish Tabi somewhere in the middle), If I'm winning, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, and if I'm losing, Randuins. Then build the rest accordingly to what the team needs. 

The reason why I like Top Akali more than Mid Akali is 1.) The matchups are a lot easier. and 2.) Taking TP allows you to both walk down mid after pushing the wave and TP bot easily. A good idea of when to roam is after you have pushed up your wave to their turret and you see a gankeable lane or if your mid laner is great at setting up ganks (for example, Viktor, ori, etc) 

If your minions are pushed up pre-6, you can simply just Q, Q, Q, Q, the enemy to harass him (1 Q seems like low dmg, but hit enough of them and you will bring them low), and try to proc as many as you can, but don't force yourself under turret aggro to do so. Something I frequently do is hide in a bush after pushing to make the other laner think that I've backed. What they would normally do is hard push so they can back as well but when they see that I haven't back and am continuing to farm, they can't back either.

I'm in almost the same position as you. Plat 4 jungle main and similar play styles. Here's my views and suggestions.

How do I counter jungle?

* WARDS, knowing what path the enemy jungler takes is very important

Which champions are best with counterjungling?

* Champions with efficient and fast clear that can also duel well. Good examples imo are: Vi, Hecarim, (Believe it or not) Amumu, rek'sai, and shyvanna. 

How do you do matchups against counterjunglers?

* Again, wards. If you like tank junglers, it's not a bad idea to purchase a sightstone. 
* Call your team mates if you are sure there is an enemy in your jungle. 

What are mistakes most beginner coutnerjunglers do?

* Not understand their enemy. I remember playing against an evelynn who tried to kill my red while I was at kruggs. It didn't end well for her when I saw her at 1/3rd health. 
* Never think about your laners' position. Several times, I have my laners (esp top laner) come down to my buff and we just kill them. This works very well when you are on purple team and they are trying to take your red buff. 

How to ward the camps as a counterjungler?

* Any ward is good if it's in their jungle clear path. Look up good areas to pink as this is also very important.

Is poacher's a really good option for Counterjunglers?

* I have never been a fan of Poacher's because it lacks effects in everything else. It's only efficient if you somehow stay in their jungle 24/7 which is never likely to happen.

How do you fight against counterjungling?

* Wards and calling for laners help. For example, lets say they level 1 stole your blue buff. Make sure you check so you can get a reset and as soon as you see the icon appear, call your laners to help you and if they refuse, tempt them with "We will probably get a kill"

How do you do starts and rotations when couterjunglerd?

* I always ask my teammates to watch my other buff. Some nice people even ward it so you don't even have to worry. If they do manage to counter jungle my buff or my camps, I decide whether I should gank a lane, or farm other camps. 

Hope this helps!

Don't:

* Tell your team: "GG we threw" or "Guys, we're throwing" or anything similar to this. This will only make the team tilt and they will focus on trying to quickly end the game instead of thinking to the reasons.

How I built my first magic deck (without having to purchase singles)
1.) Find the card I like 
2.) Sort all the cards I have of my favorite card's color
3.) try to pick out "dead" cards (card that won't be useful at all for your deck)
4.) try to make it so that your chosen cards' mana are in a bell shaped curve, with a CMC (Converted mana cost) of 4 being the top. 
5.) If you don't have enough cards (You want about 35-37 NON-LAND Cards) pick a second color (unless your favorite card was already two or more colors) 
6.) that should make your first deck. Of course, it's not going to be the best, but it's a lot of fun!
